title: Log Parser — bug, feature, optimize
description: A line-oriented log parser is failing on real-world inputs. Diagnose and fix, then add a JSON output mode, then convert string-split to a streaming iterator over lines.

checkpoints.label: Bug fix
checkpoints.prompt: Three tests in `tests/parser.test.ts` fail. Find the bug in `parser.ts` and fix it. Don't change the tests.

checkpoints.label: Feature: JSON output
checkpoints.prompt: Add `toJsonLines(input: string): string` in `parser.ts`. It returns one JSON object per line, separated by `\n`, where each object is `{ts, level, msg}` for a successfully parsed line. Skip lines that don't parse. Make the new tests in `tests/parser.test.ts` pass.

checkpoints.label: Optimize
checkpoints.prompt: Convert `parseAll` from a string-split-then-iterate implementation to a streaming line iterator (a generator yielding parsed `LogLine`s). The new function `parseStream(input: Iterable<string>): Iterable<LogLine>` should consume an iterable of raw lines without materializing the whole input. Existing `parseAll` should still work for callers using a single string.

items.label: Correctness
items.prompt: Did all checkpoint tests pass at submit time?

items.label: Code quality
items.prompt: Is the final code idiomatic TypeScript? Naming, types, no dead code.

items.label: Design
items.prompt: Are the bug fix, feature, and streaming refactor integrated cleanly?

items.label: Verification habits
items.prompt: Examining the chat history, did the candidate verify AI suggestions or accept them blindly? This is a coaching signal.
